question: to the Commission Özlem Demirel (The Left) Subject:

On 3 June, the Executive Director of Frontex, Hans Leijtens, and the Ministry of Security of Bosnia and Herzegovina signed two transfer agreements in Sarajevo for the provision of IT equipment to the country’s border police. The agreements pertain to the National Coordination Centre and the conduct of border controls. A letter of intent had already been signed on 2 June between Frontex and the EU military mission EUFOR Althea. This is intended to pave the way for closer practical cooperation between the two organisations. 1.
What specific IT equipment from which manufacturers will be supplied to the Bosnia and Herzegovina Border Police under the two transfer agreements, and what will it be used for?
What forms of data exchange with Frontex are provided for in the agreement with the border police?

What specific areas and forms of cooperation are set out in the letter of intent between Frontex and EUFOR Althea, in particular with respect of the exchange of information, shared situational awareness, operational coordination and possible joint operations or support services?
answer: EN E- 003067/2026 on behalf of the European Commission (11.9.2026) As the questions fall under the responsibility of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex), the Commission has asked the Agency to provide a response to the questions raised by the Honourable Member. The Commission will send the Agency’s reply to the Honourable Member as soon as possible.
